column1: # Words the hand-admission shape guard rejects and the Wiktionary form_of
# derivation clears. Columns: word, form_of tag (or none), base (or -).
# Why this file exists. admit-source-words.ts carries looksInflected, a cheap
# string guard meant to stop an obvious inflection being admitted by hand. The
# derivation from form_of tags is the authority; the guard is belt and braces.
# Measured over the widened candidate set they disagreed on 14 words, and the
# guard was wrong on every one of them: it rejects any -er, -ing or -s form
# whose base is itself a word, which sweeps up agent nouns (consumer, an -er
# form of consume) and gerund lemmas (clothing, a participle of clothe) that
# carry their own lemma sense and their own etymology.
# The shipped calendar already settles this. It carries 6 plural-lemma and 59
# participle-lemma crowns (evenings, mornings, offering, blessing, sleeping),
# so a guard that rejects them contradicts the standard it exists to enforce.
# The guard is wrong, not the calendar.
# So the disagreement is recorded here, word by word with its evidence, rather
# than resolved by loosening the guard's patterns until these happen to pass.
# Loosening would also wave through earliest, happiest, notified and stripped,
# which are exactly what the guard is for. A word listed here is exempt from
# the shape guard and nothing else: every other admission gate still applies.
# lemma is true for every word here, which is the whole point. A pure plural
# with no lemma sense of its own (analyses, archives) has no etymology to
# reveal, and that is what makes it unacceptable as a crown. projects is the
# deliberate case: it is tagged a plural AND carries a genuine lemma sense, so
# its reveal card shows the real etymology of project. Bea's rule was drop the
# past tense and keep everything else, and this is what that rule says.
# Derived from Wiktionary form_of tags and the lemma-sense list. Extend it by
# re-running the derivation when the candidate set widens again, not by hand.
